title: An Input-Dependent Readout Phase for Resonant Sequence Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12496v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sequence models with a fixed-size state avoid the quadratic cost of attention, but face a design choice. title: CircuitTree: Composing Circuits into A Syllable Transcriber
abstract: arXiv:2610.12520v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The goal of circuit discovery is to decompose a monolithic neural network into tiny modular subnetworks which are interpretable in the sense that each does an identifiable subtask. abstract: arXiv:2610.12527v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Distribution operators need visibility of behind-the-meter photovoltaic (PV) generation, yet most residential customers are observed only through net smart meters. abstract: arXiv:2610.12530v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Training-free feature reuse accelerates diffusion transformer inference by replacing full denoising computation at selected steps with cached approximations. abstract: arXiv:2610.12536v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: EliteTable is a self-improving program-search algorithm guided by large language models (LLMs) that uses a fixed-capacity table of high-scoring solutions to guide new proposals, edits of existing solutions, and remixes of several solutions. title: Market Impact Estimation via Causal Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12537v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a trader executes a large order, the relevant question is not \emph{what will the price be?} but \emph{what would the price have been had I not traded?} Market impact is thus a causal quantity, yet classical models (Almgren--Chriss, propagators) regress price on flow, which is biased whenever informed flow moves prices through information as well as trading. abstract: arXiv:2610.12538v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern machine learning models are typically trained on data assumed to be representative of the predictive tasks the model will face in the future, but practical datasets violate this assumption. We focus on outcome-dependent truncation in which an observation appears in the training data depending on its label. abstract: arXiv:2610.12541v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Boundary-value problems for the Laplace equation develop singular behaviour near corners, edges and junctions that smooth approximators resolve poorly. abstract: arXiv:2610.12542v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is often proposed for scheduling directed-acyclic-graph (DAG) workflows, yet most studies never run the comparison that could refute it - giving a much simpler method the same search effort. abstract: arXiv:2610.12544v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate discrete data by iteratively unmasking multiple tokens in parallel using a learned mask predictor. abstract: arXiv:2610.12545v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Autoregressive decoding is less suited to non-causally ordered data, e.g., cross-references or future dependencies, since their outputs cannot be revised post hoc, unlike iterative human reasoning. title: Sample-Adaptive Zeroth-Order Post-Training
abstract: arXiv:2610.12566v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization offers a memory-efficient alternative to backpropagation for fine-tuning large language models. abstract: arXiv:2610.12568v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.12569v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Static coding benchmarks are fixed at release. Over time their tasks leak into training data, and stronger agents eventually saturate them. We argue that a benchmark should instead aim to be self-scaling: its tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time, so no content exists in advance to leak, and its difficulty is set by the participating agents rather than fixed at release. abstract: arXiv:2610.12570v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by the target model. abstract: arXiv:2610.12574v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-teacher distillation allows transferring knowledge from multiple "teacher" networks to a single "student" network. This method is promising in fields such as digital pathology, where many powerful foundation models were proposed recently. abstract: arXiv:2610.12575v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern video-language models are increasingly treated as general-purpose video reasoners, yet it remains unclear whether they robustly capture temporal dynamics in safety-critical settings such as driving. abstract: arXiv:2610.12580v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Event ontology is the foundational framework for defining events in a dataset. Event type induction generally involves domain experts who define guidelines for creating event types and their names based on the dataset's domain and scope. abstract: arXiv:2610.12582v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A latent recurrent language model applies a shared block of layers repeatedly, so one checkpoint can trade inference compute for accuracy by changing the loop count. At one loop, however, such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a one-loop tax that makes a separate non-recurrent model the better choice whenever latency matters. abstract: arXiv:2610.12586v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Event sequences are chains of random events, each described by heterogeneous (numerical and categorical) features. The problem of event sequence forecasting occurs in finance, healthcare, business process intelligence, and other fields. abstract: arXiv:2610.12593v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The continued improvement of large language models increasingly depends on synthetic experience, yet effective data synthesis for interactive agents requires not only executable and verifiable trajectories, but also interactions that provide learning value for the current task agent. abstract: arXiv:2610.12598v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable supervision for software engineering agents through executable tests, but binary rewards fail to distinguish trajectories with substantially different debugging quality. abstract: arXiv:2610.12599v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Sparse computation can scale the parametric capacity of LLMs without proportionally increasing active computation, but pretraining sparse architectures remains expensive and data-hungry. abstract: arXiv:2610.12601v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prompt optimization is an attractive alternative to reinforcement learning for adapting language-model agents, since it is cheap and produces human-readable artifacts. On factual tasks, however, it carries a failure mode that scalar-reward reinforcement learning does not. title: Self-Preservation in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.12602v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continual learning (CL) seeks to adapt pretrained models while preserving prior capabilities. Yet the tasks supplied for preservation cover only part of what a model knows, while forgetting can extend beyond them. abstract: arXiv:2610.12617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Geopolitical and strategic intelligence reports constitute a rich source of expert knowledge and have increasing value in the current political climate, but their heterogeneity and analytical complexity pose challenges for retrieval-augmented question answering. abstract: arXiv:2610.12624v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prior outdoor LiDAR registration works are commonly limited by the pair-wise input paradigm, which neglects temporal correlations inherent within streaming sequences. abstract: arXiv:2610.12638v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Day-ahead electricity forecasts can help building operators schedule heating, ventilation, and other services around anticipated demand. abstract: arXiv:2610.12650v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When you ask a vision-language model (VLM) a question with an image, it answers your question based on the image. But to act means to choose: saying one thing means choosing to respond not say another. abstract: arXiv:2610.12651v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents executing multi-step workflows fail in two fundamentally different ways: recoverable slips, which further attempts can repair, and knowledge gaps, which retrying cannot resolve. abstract: arXiv:2610.12655v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents can execute increasingly complex tasks, but effective assistance also requires aligning their actions with goals and constraints that users may leave unstated. abstract: arXiv:2610.12657v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efficient autoregressive generation is increasingly limited by the memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length, batch size, and model depth. abstract: arXiv:2610.12659v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Data-centric scaling of RLVR has focused on collecting or generating verifiable training problems. abstract: arXiv:2610.12667v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluations on clean benchmarks overstate model robustness: real inputs arrive perturbed, and these meaning-preserving variants routinely move model answers. abstract: arXiv:2610.12668v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language model agents increasingly operate over long interaction streams, requiring online adaptation to distribution shifts through continual learning. abstract: arXiv:2610.12669v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are becoming central to GeoAI systems, yet their evaluation rarely considers the elicitation of geospatial data requirements.
